October 27, 2026
Caltech Leads NASA Mission to Make the First Deep Ultraviolet All-Sky Maps
The UVEX mission will catch the ultraviolet glow of stars, galaxies, and powerful cosmic blasts.
October 27, 2026
First Light: Celebrate the Inauguration of Caltech's 10th President, Ray Jayawardhana
Join the Caltech community on October 28 and 29 for two days of science, discovery, and celebration as the Institute welcomes a new era of leadership.
October 26, 2026
Now 90 Years Young, Caltech JPL Looks Ahead to Another Nine Decades of Innovation and Exploration
JPL has been expanding the boundaries of space exploration since 1936, and with a roster of new missions, it is poised for what comes next.
October 23, 2026
Watson Lecture: Katie Bouman Discusses Imaging the Invisible
As part of the Watson Lecture Series, Katie Bouman, professor of computing and mathematical sciences, will explain how scientific images are increasingly constructed rather than simply captured, not only in extreme astrophysics—such as through black hole imaging—but also in other disciplines.
October 15, 2026
Kareem El-Badry Wins Packard Fellowship
The astronomer is known for uncovering hidden populations of black holes

About Us
The Astronomy Department at the California Institute of Technology is part of the Division of Physics, Math, and Astronomy. The primary mission of our department is twofold: the performance of cutting-edge research in astronomy and astrophysics, including theory, observation, and experiment, as well as the education of undergraduate and graduate students and training of postdoctoral research associates who will comprise the scientists and leaders of tomorrow. We are located in the Cahill Center for Astronomy and Astrophysics on the Caltech campus.
